title: Solar Mg appendix

products.stat_basis: quantiser-floor 0.01 dex (RYA-771) — UNMEASURED: line-to-line scatter at n_lines=1; the floor STANDS IN for a scatter that was never determined, it is not a measurement of one

components.name: measurement
components.source: Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1: one line -> statistical error from the goodness of the profile fit; chi2-curvature sigma of this line, rescaled to red_chi2 = 1

evidence.likelihood: synthesis chi2 over the fit window, curvature at the best abundance
evidence.correlation_treatment: red_chi2 rescaling absorbs pixel correlation and model inadequacy; the worse-constrained side is taken

components.name: transition_data
components.source: gf covariance per data/reference/gf_error_model.csv -- MG_AGSS21: fully_correlated (scale 0.0000 dex; AGSS21 Sect. 2.4 and Table A.1; NIST ASD query 2026-10-18)

components.name: stellar.logg
components.source: solar log g is pinned; delta_logg is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.metallicity
components.source: solar [Fe/H] is pinned; delta_feh is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.teff
components.source: sourced DEFINED zero (RYA-1226 convention): the solar Teff allowance is 1 K

evidence.owed_measurement: a Teff perturbation on this pool

components.name: stellar.xi
components.source: per-line paired differential at xi 0.90/1.10 on this product's OWN pool, stamped legs (RYA-1178 A)

evidence.response_assessment: central paired mean over 1 lines; difference of aggregates 0.0250/km/s

components.name: continuum
components.source: standing continuum rule (synthesis reference, 3-MAD clipped): placement = q97 vs q80 central half-difference, REFERENCE = IAG-atlas leg minus nominal, in quadrature, paired on this pool

components.name: profile_ew
components.source: fit window +/-0.25 A core vs the band's fixed window, paired on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: MARCS.GES vs ATLAS9.Castelli, one axis varied, paired on this pool

components.name: telluric
components.source: per-line measured sky depth -> measured residual of this holding vs an independent correction on the telluric pixels -> dex via the line's own dA/df (+0.1% leg); lines independent, weight 1/n

per_line.residual_basis: solar_crires_plus_y_wide_rya1054 vs independent correction solar_kpno_molecfit_corrected, baseline-removed

components.name: blends
components.source: full atomic + molecular synthesis in-window (RYA-1230 turned molecular opacity on in every band); no catalogued-blend deficit

evidence.owed_measurement: a paired molecule-strength leg on this C/O pool

components.name: nlte
components.source: this leg applies no departures (nlte_delta_dex = 0 on every line)

components.name: pseudo_continuum
components.source: outside the near-UV the continuum is observed; it is placed per line by the standing rule and priced on `continuum`

components.name: hfs_isotopes
components.source: every pool line has hfs_n_components == 1 (canonical_gf)

components.name: molecular_coupling
components.source: atomic product; the selector is not a MOL- indicator set

components.name: holding_instrument
components.source: SynthesisHandler harness residual MEASURED against the known optical answer (RYA-869)

uncertainty.covariance_source: components independent of one another; the shared-source gf correlation lives inside transition_data
uncertainty.assumptions: solar log g and [Fe/H] pinned; Teff allowance 1 K

body_html:
Solar magnesium: 7.668 ± 0.043

Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021: 7.55 ± 0.03  ·  this measurement +0.118 dex

The three-dimensional non-LTE products apply published line-by-line corrections (Asplund et al. 2021) to our one-dimensional fits; they are not our own three-dimensional calculation. The K-band products are the first for magnesium. No second telluric correction exists in the K band, so their telluric error is scaled from the J band of the same night.

Combined the way Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse (2021) combine it: weighted mean and error of the indicator families Mg I, Mg II (Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.4); inverse total-variance weights; statistical parts combined as independent, systematic parts as shared (Amarsi+2021 Eq. 3). Each indicator is represented by our best analysis of it.

  • Mg I: 7.661 ± 0.041 · IAG FTS · red-optical · Mg I · Asplund et al. 2021 lines · 3D NLTE (Amarsi)
  • Mg II: 7.717 ± 0.106 · Kitt Peak (1984, molecfit) · NIR · Mg II · Asplund et al. 2021 lines · 3D NLTE (Amarsi)

How to read this forest. Each row is one independent product, preserving its band, holding, engine, indicator and line set. Engines and indicator families are never averaged. Each bar is the uncertainty as Asplund et al. 2021 quote it: line-to-line scatter, the 3D-model term and the NLTE term (at least 0.03 dex). Atomic-data and observational terms are not in the bar, as in Asplund; they stay in the full error budget attached to the row. Grades describe the supplied line-pool provenance, not engine quality; evaluated theoretical CNO oscillator strengths are not relabelled as laboratory evidence. Quarantined, failed and unconstrained fits have no abundance mark. Experimental products remain explicitly not adopted. Literature references provide context, never tuning targets. Yellow rows are Deep Grade: strong lines that saturate, kept but less certain than the other grades.

How this was measured

Every magnesium value on this page comes from fitting synthetic spectra to the observed solar spectrum, line by line or band by band, with the magnesium abundance as the free parameter. The synthesis includes the atomic lines and the molecular opacity in every window, so blended absorption is modelled rather than attributed to the line being measured. The continuum is placed locally around every line by comparing the observation with the synthesis on its own highest pixels, and ground-based spectra are telluric-corrected across their full range.

Each indicator is measured independently on each solar spectrum and reported separately; nothing is averaged across indicators or instruments. Where a 3D or NLTE correction is published for the lines, it is applied as its own product (1D-LTE, 1D-NLTE and 3D-NLTE are separate rows). Every value carries a full uncertainty budget: fit, line strengths, microturbulence, continuum, fit window, model atmosphere, telluric residual, and the spread between spectra, each measured by refitting with that one input changed. The headline at the top is the Asplund-grade product: a published line set, the most complete treatment, then the most lines.

Solar magnesium context

Magnesium is measured separately from neutral Mg I and ionized Mg II. Asplund et al. 2021 use eight Mg I and six Mg II features, average the lines within each ion, then weight the two ion means by their total uncertainties. Both ion results are required for the combined abundance.
